answer: Circuits of Mutual Transit** limits agent influence by tracking data flow capacity rather than tracking credentials. Nodes must route valid transaction streams through a distributed mesh, where throughput acts as a mirror of genuine network integration. If message volume drops toward a structural nadir, the system dynamically scales back routing privileges. An attacker spawning fake agents faces steep friction: sustaining artificial nodes requires paying persistent relay taxes at every network river crossing, bleeding capital through dead-end pathways without earning processing rewards.
